newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Mundial Confianca sees no capital call.
newsitem.headline: Mundial Confianca sees no capital call.

text.p: Insurer Mundial Confianca denied on Thursday a press report that it might have to make a capital call to comply with proposed new legislation on debt levels.
"No capital call is foreseen, nor would one be necessary under the terms of the law," Mundial Confianca finance director Paulo Vasconcelos told Reuters.
Vasconcelos said that Mundial Confianca's debt level would be below the limits laid down by the time the law came into effect.

Debt currently stood at 25 billion escudos ($158.7 million) against the 23.5 billion indicated as the upper level under the terms of the proposed law. But the company had the means to redeem up to five billion escudos of debt before the end of the year, he said.
The new legislation, proposed by the Portuguese Insurance Institute, would set an upper debt limit of 40 percent of net worth.
